pairs.evidence: src/lib/settleThread.test.ts:195 The context's one source-scan gate (blocking: vitest runs in CI) asserts a property, that badge counts are not import-time constants, by matching two literal identifiers in raw source text, so renaming the constant clears the check while the pass still claims the property holds.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/settleThread.test.ts:195 The key is a name the author controls: MOCK_HEALTH_ALERTS / MOCK_OPEN_INCIDENTS on lines 198-199. Reintroducing an import-time constant under any other name passes. The test title states the property ('are no longer import-time constants') instead of 'no listed token found', so this floor reports itself as a ceiling.

src/lib/settleThread.test.ts:190 The presence assertion runs a regex over raw readFileSync text (line 189) that was never normalised to executing code. A commented-out import line, or one whose binding is never called, satisfies 'has a production importer'. The absence assertions on 198-199 also have no presence assertion for the replacement (e.g. healthAlertCount being the badge's source).

src/lib/settleThread.test.ts:192 The walked population `sources` (line 185) is shared with the absence test. This positive control fails if the walk returns zero files or misses mockApi.ts, so the for-loop absence check at 196 cannot pass vacuously over an empty walk without the sibling test going red.
